big_idea: Math is everywhere in our community: parks, hockey rinks, libraries, restaurants.
learning_intention: We are learning to describe a community situation and ask a math question about it.
student_learning_goal: I can describe a community situation and ask a math question about it.
success_criteria: I can name 3+ community locations with math.
I can ask a math question about a community situation.
I can tell math questions apart from descriptive questions.
lesson_specific_materials: OPTIONAL: Coach Cara — if available; otherwise teacher voices both characters in two distinct voices, or substitutes two stuffed animals / paper-bag puppets / pictures on the anchor poster. Activity is unaffected.
Lesson 1 question tracker — provided in assessment_suite stage

minds_on.hook: Coach Cara: Math is everywhere in our community! Where do you see math? Coach Cara opens: 'math questions ANSWER WITH NUMBERS!'
minds_on.teacher_script:
Bring children to the carpet. Coach Cara puppet. 'Friends — I'm Coach Cara the Community Captain. Today we see math everywhere in our community.'

Introduce vocabulary. Write MODEL and REAL-LIFE SITUATION on chart. 'A model is a math representation. We pick a situation, ask a math QUESTION, and find the answer.'

Show the community map. Point to hockey rink. 'How many goals scored in a season?' Park: 'How many trees?' Library: 'How many books in the children's section?' Restaurant: 'How many pizzas sold per Saturday?'

'These are MATH questions. They start with HOW MANY, HOW MUCH, HOW LONG. They have NUMBER answers.'

Contrast with descriptive: 'What's the colour of the rink? Not math. What flavour pizza? Not math.'

More math examples:
- How many goals scored at the rink in 1 month?
- How many books returned to the library on Friday?
- How many people on the bus at 8am?
- How long is the bridge to walk?
- How many TTC trips per week?

'Coach Cara says — pick a community LOCATION, ask a math QUESTION. That's how we start a model.'

'Today we identify community math and ask questions.'
student_actions: Suggest math questions for community locations.

steps.instruction: Whole group: pick 4 community locations. Suggest 2 math questions for each.
steps.teacher_prompt: Say: 'Math questions start with HOW. Suggest 2 each.'

steps.instruction: Three stations. Station A: Community Map — pair picks 4 locations and writes 2 math questions for each. Station B: Sort — pair sorts 12 question cards into MATH and NOT MATH. Station C: Make Your Own — pair writes 4 of their own community math questions.
Stretch challenge at Station C: write a question that needs 2 numbers (e.g., difference between weekday and weekend visitors).
Discuss math vs descriptive. 'Math questions feed the modelling cycle. Descriptive questions are great too, but for a different purpose.'
Circulate to record formative evidence on the question tracker.
steps.teacher_prompt: Stop at each pair. Ask 'Math question for the rink?' Mark the tracker.

steps.instruction: STRATEGY COMPARE: Two pairs share questions about the same location (rink, library, store). Class compares: which is MOST answerable with a count? Cite English & Watters (2005) — modelling questions partition by operational tag.
steps.teacher_prompt: Coach Cara: 'Same location, different math. The QUESTION decides the tool.'

differentiation.for_emerging: Stay at Station A. Use familiar locations.
differentiation.for_ell_or_iep: Provide a structured frame: 'How many ___ at the ___?'
differentiation.for_movement_learners: Walk around the room as if it's the community.

formative_check.what_to_look_for: Three signals: identifies locations; writes math questions; distinguishes math from descriptive.

discussion_prompts: What's a community location with math?
consolidation.exit_routine: Coach Cara's refrain — class chants: 'Coach Cara's rule: math questions ANSWER WITH NUMBERS!' (3x). Each child writes one math question + tag (COUNT/MEASURE/PREDICT) on a sticky.

assessment_in_this_lesson.rationale: Lesson 1 surfaces children who already grasp math questions vs those who default to descriptive.

expanded_walkthrough.title: When the child writes 'What sport is best?' instead of a math question — repairing the descriptive-vs-math at Grade 3 community scale
expanded_walkthrough.rationale:
On real-world community math questions, the Grade-3 trap is opinion-vs-math confusion: child writes 'why is the rink fun?' instead of 'how many ice times per week?' English & Watters (2005, 'Mathematical Modelling in the Early School Years') and Lesh's model-eliciting activities place math-question framing as the gateway to all later modelling.

Today: math questions about community locations. Tomorrow Cara tallies counts (Lesson 2 — C4.1). Lesson 3 predictions; Lesson 4 reflections; Lesson 5 capstones.
expanded_walkthrough.setup: Pair is at Station A. Map shows a restaurant. Child writes 'What's the best food at the restaurant?'.
expanded_walkthrough.teacher_script:
Crouch. 'Great curiosity question. But Coach Cara needs a MATH question. Math questions have NUMBER answers.'

Walk through. 'Try: HOW MANY people eat at the restaurant on Friday? HOW MUCH does a meal cost? HOW LONG does it take to make a pizza? Each is a number.'

The child rewrites. Generalise. 'Coach Cara says — math questions start with HOW. They produce NUMBERS, not opinions.'

If still opinion-based: provide HOW frame card. 'HOW MANY ___ at the ___?' Force the math start.

Long-term recovery: every modelling task starts with HOW.
common_misconceptions: Any question is a math question. (Repair: math questions have number answers.)
Opinions are math too. (Repair: opinions are not measurable.)
I can't think of math questions. (Repair: use HOW frames.)
recovery_moves: DIAGNOSTIC A — child writes opinion ('why is fun?'): drill 'math questions ANSWER WITH NUMBERS'; child rewrites with HOW MANY/HOW MUCH/HOW LONG.
DIAGNOSTIC B — child writes math but unanswerable ('how many stars?'): drill 'COUNTABLE' constraint; child re-checks.
DIAGNOSTIC C — child writes good question but won't categorise: model COUNT/MEASURE/PREDICT on 3 sample questions; child sorts.

parts_outline.task: Describe a community location in 2-3 sentences.
Write 4 math questions about the community.
Sort 6 questions into MATH and NOT MATH.
